ordered_diagnoses: Solid and cystic hidradenoma with malignant transformation

s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent lesion of the nasal vestibule with local invasion
salient_findings: Recurrent lesion of the right nasal vestibule mucosa
Tumor within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
key_facts: Female patient in her 50s
Never-smoker
Initial lesion biopsied 5 years prior
Initial biopsy reported as solid and cystic hidradenoma
p63 positive, pancytokeratin positive, and p16 negative on initial biopsy
Lesion recurred 8 months prior to presentation
Second excision showed p63 positive and p16 negative with positive margins
Enlarged, firm right ala on examination
Tumor visualized within the nasal vestibule floor and ala
Imaging showed thicker right ala compared to the left ala

raw.rationale: The patient's initial biopsy was reported as a solid and cystic hidradenoma, but the recurrence and aggressive behavior of the lesion, as well as the positive margins on the second excision, suggest malignant transformation, which is consistent with hidradenocarcinoma.

rejected.label: Squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The initial biopsy was p16 negative, which is not typical for squamous cell carcinoma, and the histological description does not match squamous cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Basal cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's lesion does not have the typical characteristics of basal cell carcinoma, such as a pearly nodule or ulceration, and the histological description does not match basal cell carcinoma.

rejected.label: Adenoid cystic carcinoma
rejected.why: The histological description does not match adenoid cystic carcinoma, which typically has a cribriform or tubular pattern, and the patient's lesion does not have the typical characteristics of adenoid cystic carcinoma.

rejected.label: Solid and cystic hidradenoma with malignant transformation
rejected.why: While this option is close, hidradenocarcinoma is a more specific diagnosis that better explains the patient's aggressive and recurrent lesion.
